name: Bald Knobber graves: Dave & Billy Walker
where: Abundance Cemetery, near Sparta, Christian County. I could not find coordinates for the cemetery, so the circle is centered on Sparta.
story: Father and son hanged with John Mathews in Ozark on May 10, 1889, after a botched gallows. The last act of the Christian County Bald Knobbers.
access: Cemetery access unknown. Ask the landowner if it's on private land.
search: "Abundance Cemetery" Sparta Christian County

sources.t: Missouri Gravestones: David Walker
Geocache GCX6XY (notes graves near Sparta)

name: Mathews Cemetery (John Mathews lead)
where: Mathews Cemetery near Chadwick, Christian County (USGS coordinates).
story: UNCONFIRMED LEAD. John Mathews was the third Bald Knobber hanged in 1889, and the Christian County group was centered on Chadwick. I found no source saying where he is buried. This family cemetery is a lead, not a match.
search: John Mathews Bald Knobber buried

sources.t: Bald Knobbers (Wikipedia)

name: Snapp Balds: Bald Knobbers' first meeting place
where: Just north of Kirbyville, Taney County. USGS marks Snapp Balds as a ridge range; the exact meeting knob isn't pinned.
story: Where Nat Kinney's Taney County vigilantes first met. The open bald knobs let them watch for spies, and gave the group its name.
search: Snapp Bald Bald Knobbers Kirbyville

sources.t: Bald Knobbers (Wikipedia)

name: Murder Rock: Alf Bolin's ambush spot
where: Limestone outcrops on Pine Mountain beside the old Springfield–Harrison road, about 10 miles south of Forsyth, Taney County (USGS coordinates). A 1974 account says Highway JJ runs about 60 ft east of the old roadbed, and Coal Pit Hollow spring sits at the foot of the mountain.
story: Civil War bushwhacker Alf Bolin reportedly hid in these rocks to rob and kill travelers on the road. Look for the old roadbed beside it in the LiDAR.
access: PRIVATE. Owner proposed public access in 2020; status unknown since. Don't go without permission.
search: Murder Rock Alf Bolin Taney County

sources.t: KY3: Murder Rock could open to the public (2020)
White River Valley Hist. Quarterly: Alf Bolin's Buried Treasure (1974)

name: Layton's Mill: where Alf Bolin was killed
where: About 3 miles south of Murder Rock, near the Arkansas line. The circle is placed from that distance alone.
story: An 1862 Union report put Bolin's band in the hills toward 'Laten's Mills'. A disguised Union soldier killed Bolin with a plow colter at the nearby home of Mrs. Foster. His head was later put on a pole in Ozark. Mill and house are long gone.
search: Layton Mill Taney County Alf Bolin

sources.t: Ozarks History: Alf Bolin, just facts
White River Valley Hist. Quarterly: Alf Bolin's Buried Treasure (1974)

name: Clark's Mill battle & blockhouse
where: On Bryant Creek about a mile north of Vera Cruz, Douglas County. Placed from that description.
story: Union blockhouse captured and destroyed in the Nov. 7, 1862 battle. A 2012 report says traces of the old Vera Cruz Road are still visible on the farm. Good LiDAR target.
search: Clark's Mill battle Vera Cruz Douglas County

sources.t: Battle of Clark's Mill (Wikipedia)
KSMU: landowner finds his farm was a battle site (2012)

name: Vera Cruz: lost first county seat
where: On Bryant Creek, central Douglas County (USGS coordinates).
story: Douglas County's first seat until 1870, with a courthouse, mills, blacksmith and about 15 homes. Now only a cemetery and an old log church remain. Building pads and the old mill pond may show in LiDAR.
search: Vera Cruz Douglas County Missouri history

sources.t: Vera Cruz, Missouri (Wikipedia)
KSMU (2012)

name: Breadtray Mountain: Spanish silver legend
where: Summit near Table Rock Lake, Stone County (USGS coordinates). The legend gives no spot on the mountain.
story: Centuries-old tale of Spanish explorers sealing a silver mine here. Unproven. Old prospect pits or diggings might show on the slope layer.
access: Ownership not checked. Confirm before going; no digging on public land.
search: Breadtray Mountain Spanish silver legend

sources.t: State of the Ozarks: Legend of Breadtray Mountain
KY3: Buried treasure in the Ozarks

name: Alf Bolin's lost grave
where: Right side of the old Swan Creek Road, about 1 mile north and east of Old Forsyth (now Shadowrock Park), Taney County. Circle placed from that description.
story: After his head was cut off, the outlaw's body was buried in an unmarked grave. The one witness, a boy of 12 at the time, could never pinpoint it later. Look for the old Swan Creek roadbed in the LiDAR.
access: Mixed private and public land. Unmarked grave: don't dig.
search: Alf Bolin grave Forsyth Swan Creek road

sources.t: White River Valley Hist. Quarterly: Alf Bolin's Buried Treasure (1974)

name: Alf Bolin's treasure cave
where: Fox Creek Hills, Section 20, T22N R20W, about 2 miles southwest of the old Mincy store and mill, Taney County. Circle is that section's center.
story: Bolin's loot is said to be buried near a cave in these hills. A stranger spent several summers searching from a farm on Highway JJ and never said whether he found it.
access: Ownership not checked. Confirm before going.
search: Alf Bolin treasure Fox Creek Mincy cave

sources.t: White River Valley Hist. Quarterly: Alf Bolin's Buried Treasure (1974)

name: Murder Rocks Union soldiers' graves
where: About 3 miles south of Kirbyville, on what was the Charley Mahnkey place in 1974, Taney County. Circle placed from distance only.
story: Two Union soldiers ambushed at Murder Rocks were buried here. No marker is described.
search: Union soldiers buried Mahnkey Kirbyville Murder Rocks

sources.t: White River Valley Hist. Quarterly: Alf Bolin's Buried Treasure (1974)

name: Smallett Cave: the Headless Cobbler
where: Near Smallett, Douglas County. Spring Creek runs just north of the cave mouth, close to the Glade Top Trail. Circle is centered on Smallett.
story: A Civil War cobbler, believed to be Wesley Evans, hid in the cave to work out of sight of bushwhackers. People report a headless figure on the back roads at dusk, tapping inside the cave, a red light, and phantom horses.
access: Ownership unknown; nearby road may be private.
search: Smallett Cave headless cobbler Douglas County

sources.t: Ozarks Alive: Headless Cobbler of Smallett Cave

name: Blue Man of Spring Creek: 1865 sighting
where: North slope of 'Upper Twin Mountain', site of the first sighting in 1865. Pinned on USGS Twin Mountain (Howell County, near the Douglas line). Likely the same mountain but NOT confirmed.
story: Hairy wild man said to roam the Spring Creek, North Fork and Indian Creek hills from the 1860s. A 1911 posse reportedly found his den full of animal bones. Its location was never recorded.
search: Blue Man Spring Creek Ozarks legend den

sources.t: Ozarks Alive: The Blue Man
Howell County News: When the Blue Man roamed

name: Garrison Cave: treasure & skeleton
where: About 1 mile east of Ozark, below the old Garrison homestead on a hilltop near a bluff, Christian County. Circle placed from that description.
story: In 1853 a stranger with a divining rod said treasure was buried in the cave. Diggers quit twice over ghostly sounds. A later dig found ashes, slag, bones and a human skeleton, but no treasure.
search: Garrison Cave Ozark Missouri treasure

sources.t: Ozarks' History: Gold in Ozark Hills (1893 article)

name: Devil's Den: the 'bottomless' sinkhole
where: Water-filled sinkhole in an oak grove west of Fordland, Webster County (USGS coordinates).
story: Said never to have been sounded, with a water level that rises and falls about 30 ft. In the late 1800s it had a ladder, railing and band platform for social gatherings. The owner who bought it in 1980 later stopped allowing visitors.
search: Devil's Den Webster County Fordland sinkhole

sources.t: Ozarks Alive: Devil's Den

name: Parson Keithly's hidden gold
where: Near Galena, Stone County. Keithley's Cave near the family land, where he built a rock-walled tomb room. Cave not located; wide circle around Galena.
story: A preacher came back from the California gold rush with about $6,000 in gold and hid it. His family never found it. Suspects: the cave, or under an apple tree in a far garden.
search: Parson Keithly gold Keithley Cave Galena

sources.t: Legends of America: Parson Keithly's Hidden Gold

name: Dewey's lost lead cave
where: Side of Dewey Bald, just east of the Stone–Taney line (USGS summit coordinates; the cave's side of the mountain isn't given). The summit itself is now developed.
story: Captain Sam Dewey, a hermit and government agent among the Delaware, supposedly mined nearly pure lead from a cave here. He hid the entrance under a flat rock covered with dirt. The 1923 writer hunted for it as a boy and never found it. A burned cabin site was said to be on top.
access: Mostly private land. Ownership not checked.
search: Dewey Bald cave lead Sam Dewey legend

sources.t: WRV Quarterly: Waldo Powell, Dewey Bald Legend (1923, reprinted 1978)

name: Table Rock Bluff blockhouse
where: Table Rock bluff near the mouth of Fall Creek on the White River, Taney County (USGS 'Table Rock' summit). Settlers also smelted lead at Slick Rock Ford on Fall Creek.
story: Settlers reportedly built blockhouses on a narrow point of this bluff, with a spring inside, as a fort in case of trouble with the Delaware. Barricade lines or building pads could show on LiDAR if the story is true.
access: Near Table Rock Dam; ownership not checked.
search: Table Rock bluff blockhouse Fall Creek Dewey settlers

sources.t: WRV Quarterly: Dewey Bald Legend

name: Kirbyville picnic spring shootout
where: A spring at the Kirbyville picnic ground, Taney County. Circle is centered on Kirbyville; the spring isn't located.
story: July 4, 1889: the Miles brothers shot Sheriff Galba Branson and detective Ed Funk in front of about 100 picnickers, then escaped into the brush. The fallout from the Bald Knobber era.
search: Kirbyville picnic 1889 Branson Funk Miles spring

sources.t: WRV Quarterly: Willful Murder (1889 news reprint)
Bald Knobbers (Wikipedia)

name: Younger's Cave, Monegaw Springs
where: Bluff above the Osage River near Monegaw Springs, St. Clair County. Pinned on USGS 'Youngers Lookout'; the cave isn't separately mapped.
story: Cole Younger is said to have hidden out in a bluff cave here while family and friends lived nearby. Farther from you than the rest, but still in the Ozarks.
search: Younger cave Monegaw Springs Cole Younger

sources.t: Missouri State Archives: Caves in History and Legend

name: Yocum silver & the 'Spanish fort'
where: Galena / lower James River area, Stone County. Very wide circle: no source gives a usable spot.
story: Legend says Spaniards cached silver in caves here and the Yocum family later minted 'Yocum dollars' from it. One searcher claimed to find foundation stones of a small Spanish fort; another found a rock painting of a human figure on a creek bed. Historians doubt the whole story.
access: Lower areas are under Table Rock Lake.
search: Yocum silver dollar Spanish fort rock painting Galena

sources.t: WRV Quarterly: Legendary Hidden Silver (1978)
WRV Quarterly: Yocum Silver Dollar, Fact or Legend?

name: Brown's Cave & the 'Devil's Gulch'
where: Bryant Creek about 2 miles downstream from the mouth of Rippee Creek, about 6 miles from Vera Cruz, Douglas County. Placed from that description. Entrance is 20–30 ft above the creek on a steep, rugged hill.
story: A big cave that a 1957 county history says was never fully explored. A second section about 1.5 miles in has a deep chasm called the 'Devil's Gulch.' Methodists held meetings inside in 1892, and old-timers told stories about it.
access: Ownership not checked. Rippee State Wildlife Management Area (USGS name) is nearby; check the boundary.
search: Brown's Cave Bryant Creek Douglas County

Dr. Brown's Excerpts of the Douglas County Herald, 1887–99 (PDF)

name: Fort Lawrence (Beaver Station)
where: Beaver Creek at Rome, Douglas County. Built to guard Lawrence Mill. Circle centered on Rome.
story: Union militia blockhouse guarding the mill and the Forsyth road. Confederates under Emmett McDonald surprised and burned it on Jan. 7, 1863, the day before the Battle of Springfield. Family legend says a log cabin from the fort was moved to Ava.
search: Fort Lawrence Beaver Station Rome Missouri 1863

Ozarks History: Skirmish at Ft. Lawrence

name: Thornfield 'volcano' cave (1899)
where: Bill Trent's farm, about 2 miles north of Thornfield, Ozark County. Placed from that distance.
story: In 1899 smoke poured out of a plowed field for three days. A hole had blown open, and men who went in found a large cave in what looked like a bed of onyx. Cause never explained in the paper.
search: Thornfield Missouri cave smoke 1899 Trent onyx

sources.t: Dr. Brown's Excerpts of the Douglas County Herald, 1887–99 (PDF)

name: Indian money cave, Clay Township
where: Somewhere in Clay Township, northeastern Douglas County. Very wide circle centered on the township.
story: An 1892 Herald correspondent wrote that an old Indian came through saying his tribe had hidden a large amount of money in a cave here. The writer joked that if you don't find the money you might find lead.
search: Douglas County Missouri Indian money cave legend

sources.t: Dr. Brown's Excerpts of the Douglas County Herald, 1887–99 (PDF)

name: Pennington's lead mine
where: About 2 miles east of Ava, Douglas County. Placed from that distance.
story: Capt. E. D. Pennington leased out his lead mine here in the 1890s. Old shafts and spoil piles are good LiDAR targets. Not a legend, but a forgotten site.
access: Private land likely. Old shafts are dangerous.
search: Pennington lead mine Ava Missouri

sources.t: Dr. Brown's Excerpts of the Douglas County Herald, 1887–99 (PDF)

name: Jordan Creek sealed Spanish cave
where: Jordan Creek near where it joins a larger creek, Springfield (pinned at USGS Jordan Creek mouth). Railroad construction reportedly sealed the entrance.
story: 1858 letters and maps described a cave sealed with a flat stone marked with a turkey track, holding Spanish bullion. People dug for decades into the 1930s.
search: Jordan Creek Springfield Spanish cave turkey track

sources.t: Ozarks First: The long hunt for hidden gold and treasure in the Ozarks

name: Ash Cave: Civil War gold
where: Near Cassville, Barry County. Cave not located; wide circle centered on Cassville.
story: Gold said to be hidden from bushwhackers, or stolen from a stagecoach on the Old Wire Road. 1920s diggers went 25–30 ft into crevices and found only arrowheads.
search: Ash Cave Cassville gold Old Wire Road
